source.title: Representations in vision and language converge in a shared, multidimensional space of perceived similarities
source.authors: K. M. Simkova; Adrien Doerig; Clayton Hickey; Ian Charest

record.tranche_reason: The study reports cross-modal similarity among human judgments and their fit to brain and computational-model representations, but it does not test whether independently trained AI models become more similar as their scale or capability increases, or any other listed claim version.
record.gate_note: The human visual-versus-linguistic RDM correlations and the brain/model fit results are related evidence about representational similarity, but they do not measure convergence between AI models of the kind named in the claim versions. The paper's references to other studies are not recorded as results.
record.test_reason: The study measures cross-modal alignment of human similarity judgements (images vs captions), their fit to fMRI RDMs, and which models (LLM-trained RCNN, category-trained RCNN, AlexNet, MPNet) best fit human behavioural geometry. It never compares the representations of independently trained AI models to each other. It does not vary model scale or capability, and it does not measure cross-seed feature sharing, model-to-model mapping, or recurring features. Model-to-human/brain fit is a related but different construct, so no claim version is tested. Huh et al. 2024 is cited only as motivation.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is largely right. The authors conclude that human visual and linguistic similarity judgements share a modality-agnostic relational structure that mirrors visual-cortex encoding, even before exposure to the other modality. They add that LLM-trained RCNNs best capture this structure, outperforming category-trained RCNNs and AlexNet.
record.recipe_differences: Not a reproduction of either original source's model-to-model convergence analysis. The study uses human multiple-arrangement judgments, brain-RDM prediction, and comparisons of model fit to behavioral RDMs.
record.method_sensitivity: The study reports separate fixed-effects and random-effects estimates and compares NNLS-based brain prediction with direct RDM correlation; these are analyses of human behavioral-to-brain alignment, not sensitivity tests of AI-model convergence.

fits_no_version.finding: Averaged human visual and linguistic similarity RDMs for 100 NSD images/captions correlate strongly (fixed effects ρ=0.781; random effects ρ=0.161).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Human similarity judgements of scenes and their captions share representational geometry.

fits_no_version.finding: Visual and linguistic behavioural RDMs predict fMRI RDMs in mid/high-level visual cortex to a similar degree (peaks 0.363/0.353). This holds with Session 1 data and with direct correlation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Human visual and linguistic similarity structures both predict visually evoked brain geometry.

fits_no_version.finding: Human behavioural RDMs fit LLM-trained RCNNs better than category-trained RCNNs (layer 4 onward) and better than AlexNet. They fit MPNet better for linguistic judgements but worse for visual ones.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Vision models trained to predict LLM caption embeddings better match human similarity structure than category-trained models.

record.code_released: not stated; the text says behavioral data and analysis code will be available upon publication
record.problems: The results are indirect evidence for the catalog claim: they do not measure AI-model convergence. The behavioral dataset contains 63 participants and 100 image-caption pairs; the fMRI analysis uses 8 participants. No model-size or capability sweep is reported. Several model-fit values are presented only in figures.

untested.parts: No comparison of AI models' representations with each other across scale or capability.
Cross-modal alignment is measured only in human judgements. No vision-model vs language-model alignment is reported, and model quality is not varied.
RCNNs were trained with 10 seeds, but cross-seed similarity is never reported; seeds are only averaged.
No mapping or stitching between models.
No feature- or circuit-level comparison across models.
No sensitivity of model-to-model similarity to metric or data.
No measure of the completeness or causes of model-to-model alignment.

missing.what: Comparisons of the LLM-trained RCNN with AlexNet and with MPNet embeddings (fit to behaviour-predicted RDMs). The RCNN beats AlexNet in both modalities; it beats MPNet in the visual modality but not the linguistic one. These bear on no version.
missing.locator: Results, LLM-trained visual ANNs; Supplementary Figures 8, 9

record.verdict_notes: The title's 'converge' refers to human vision and language judgements, not to AI models. The Platonic Representation Hypothesis is cited only as interpretive context.

versions.untested_parts: No independently trained AI models are compared for representational alignment across model sizes or capability levels.
The study compares human judgments about paired images and captions, not vision and language models, and does not vary model performance.
Ten random seeds are used for RCNNs, but the study does not measure shared features or subspaces across seeds.
No mapping, stitching, relative-representation, or unpaired alignment between models is tested.
The study does not test recurrence of interpretable features or circuits across models.
The study uses different analyses and modalities, but does not test whether AI-model convergence depends on similarity metrics, settings, or input distributions.
The study does not measure the completeness or plateau of alignment between AI models, or test shared training data or objectives as causes of such alignment.
